steps.text: Preheat the oven to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C).
Cut the pumpkin into several pieces that fit comfortably in the roasting pan. Remove the stringy pulp, reserving the edible seeds for roasting, if desired.
Place cut pumpkin, skin-side up, in a large roasting pan. Add 1/4 inch of water.
Bake in the preheated oven, uncovered, until the flesh is very soft and can be pierced easily with a fork or the tip of a knife, about 1 hour. Remove from the oven and let cool for 10 to 20 minutes.
Cut the skin away from the cooled pumpkin pieces. Transfer the pumpkin flesh to a food processor and purée until smooth, or mash it in a bowl with a potato masher.

raw_recipe.headline: Cooked Pumpkin
raw_recipe.description: Learn how to cook pumpkin by roasting a fresh sugar pumpkin and turning it into smooth homemade purée for pies, soups, breads, and more.

review.reviewBody: This is exactly how I cook my pumpkins. The only thing I will chime in with is that as long as the pumpkin will fit in your bakind dish, and in your oven, there is no reason to cut it first. Save yourself some fingers, and after puncturing it a few times with a fork, bake it whole until it is tender enough to stab through with a fork. Then allow it to cool before you cut it in half. You will find cutting it to be much easier, and often the stem will pull right off.

I’ve been using fresh pumpkin for my pies for decades. I always bake the whole pumpkin until it’s soft. The time required depends on the size of the pumpkin. It’s so much easier! The stem comes right off and then I cut the baked pumpkin in half. I scoop out the seeds and fibrous material first. Then I scoop out the flesh and put it in a blender or food processor. Easy Peasy. It makes the best pumpkin pies! The texture is smooth and creamy, and it has so much more flavor.

I cook with fresh pumpkin all the time. In my house it is just another winter squash. BUT I cook it the same way I cook all winter squashes, whole with some holes poked in it IN THE MICROWAVE. Usually takes 5 minutes depending on the size. let cool, cut, scoop out seeds, separate from shell. Also freezes at this point.
I used kabocha squash, my favorite (it later became a soup). I start by placing the entire pumpkin in the oven for about 10 minutes, this softens the skin and makes it easier to cut it.

I cook my pumpkin in the microwave. Buy small cooking pumpkins that will fit into your microwave. Wash the skin with soap and hot water. Cut two small holes all the way through into the hollow right next to the stem. Microwave full power 10 minets, turn the pumpkin and repeat the process until the skin is loose and leathery. (A pumpkin about the size of your smallest mixing bowl in a standard set, will take 30 min. and render 4 to 5 cups of pulp).
Let the whole pumpkin stand for 10 min. before cutting in half. (the steam will burn you so use protection when you cut). Remove with a spoon all the guts and seeds. The pumpkin is then easly scooped and scraped out of the skin. I love this method because there is very little waste. The seeds are still good to process for snacking.

Super easy! Fresh, cooked pumpkin makes such a difference. Once mashed, freezes well. I did NOT cut up. Just poked some holes and bake whole. It is done when you press on it and it is soft and the stem pulls out pretty easily. Let cool, then cut in half, scoop out seeds and enjoy the sweet pumpkin goodness. Thanks!

I cooked a whole squash the other day without cutting it up at all. It was fabulous. I simply baked till soft and then cut it in half and cleaned it and let it sit till cool. No cutting chopping or peeling. Try it, you'll love it!

I loved how easy this was to cook! But I used someone else's idea and baked it whole! My daughter had cooked another pumpkin and she said it was really hard to cut the pumpkin first. It was so easy to scoop out the pumpkin. I only had enough for 1 pie. But it tasted delicious. There was no extra water so I didn't have to squeeze out any water!
After mashing, DRAIN the pumpkin. Easier to bake with.

I just used a cookie sheet to put the pumpkin on. I let the pumpkin cool a good 2-3 hours. When I grabbed the pumpkin to turn it over the skin just came off in my hand! No scooping! Couldn't be easier and could have cut through the pumpkin with a spoon. Pureed in no time. No more anxiety over preparing pumpkin for recipes. Only cuts were to remove the top (stem) and cut in half.

I like easy, put the washed pumpkin whole in the oven with holes punched in it, And when done pull the seeds out and get rid of the hooey-gooey strings. Bake the seeds and fix the pumpkin as you like.

Great simple recipe we've used for years now and freeze the pumpkin puree for the year so we can make muffins, risotto, pies, dog treats, etc. Love all of the recommendations made by others!!! Much appreciated!
easy method but it does take time-- feel free to adjust based on what type of pumpkin you have-- smaller chunks cook faster! I would also forgo the water-- pumpkins are SO wet.

Cut into manageable pieces? Why? I had never cooked pumpkin before, so I just did what it said. I have cooked other squash - and I have always just halved it and cooked it.

When it took longer to cook than the recipe said, I looked at some other recipes on line. ALL of them said to half the pumpkin.

Manageable pieces. Ugh!!!! There was nothing manageable about them. I had to cut more and peel more. I hope people read my review before they cook pumpkin in this ridiculous way.
The only thing I do differently is use a crockpot.
I used this to make fresh pumpkin pie and it was perfect!

I tried cooking a pumpkin whole for the first time. It took more than an hour (but it was larger than a pie pumpkin). When it was done I could cut it in quarters with a fork! I let it cool a bit for easier handling, and to my pleasant surprise it's easier to separate the fiber and seeds from the cooked pumpkin flesh than the raw. One tip: if you let your pumpkin cool, the liquid will run out. Pour some of that liquid into the food processor to get your pumpkin to perfect consistency.

I love this easy simple recipe. Followed another reviewers advice and put half a pumpkin (which i stabbed with a knife a few times) skin side up and baked at 150' C for 1.5 hrs. Important to remember to add some water too the baking pan. Thanks for sharing the recipe!
worked like a charm.
Easy...I forgot to add water, and it was ok anyhow
